role: strengthening: replace case-by-case thin-family proofs by one uniform (Milin-like) statement that implies them all, and ideally ES
missing_theorem: Uniform thin-family theorem: for every fixed (a, b, c) with b ≥ 2 and n_s = a·b^s + c, there are an exponent budget B(a,b,c) and a finite set of window templates (Sophie-Germain / moving-gap cubic type) such that every n_s has a Type I/II solution with window exponent ≤ B — in particular the open families 15·2^s + 1, 4^s + 297, 4^s + 33, 4^s + 273. The Milin analogue for primes (a strengthened uniform statement implying ES) is H⁻_BM.
yield: partial (ES on all exponential families a·b^s + c; nothing for a general prime)
status_ref: Proved families: (J)62, (J)69, (J)74, (J)75, (J)80 (FRONTIER §1 'Thin infinite families'); 3·2^s+1, 7·4^s+9, 63·2^s+1 admit no finite ET covering ((J)22 Cor 1.5, (J)68 Lemma 3.1) and are won by factorisation-forced budgets; open ones FRONTIER §7.8; (J)102 (15·2^s+1 II-ad branch sterile). Transfer to primes blocked: (J)76 (menu ladder collapses to B1/B2), (J)84 Thm A (no algebraic budget at a general prime unless p = φ(u))
barrier: B1 for the family (no finite covering) — escaped in proved cases by p-dependent windows forced by algebraic factorisations (E1); for primes: (J)84 irreducibility, B2
new_ingredient: none (the common mechanism — an algebraic factorisation of the family polynomial supplying a forced window — is the repo's own)
next: Tabulate, for the proved families, which polynomial identity in X = b^s supplies the window (4X⁴+1 Sophie Germain, cubic class); test whether 15·2^s + 1 admits any such identity in X = 2^s up to degree 6 (exhaustive small-coefficient search) — a negative result would show the uniform statement needs a non-algebraic ingredient.
note: Milin's lesson was 'prove a stronger, better-behaved statement'. For ES the only repo-level strengthening of that kind is H⁻_BM, which is ES-strength (circular); the thin-family uniformisation is a genuine but ES-irrelevant research problem.

BREADTH_Z45 §1 (transfer_logic, PROVED): for monic ES_q at fixed degree success proportion is O_d(q^{−k}), 'successes structured, failures generic' — the FF limit cannot be interchanged with ES; FRONTIER §6 'ultraproduct transfer'

role: relaxation (one numerator-2 term, repeated denominators allowed) then transport back to three unit fractions
missing_theorem: Transport theorem: from 4/n = 2/((n+1)/2) + 1/M + 1/M (M = n(n+1)/2) produce a 3-unit-fraction representation. The 2/y term splits only as 1/y + 1/y (4 terms) or merges only when y is even, i.e. (n+1)/2 even ⟺ n ≡ 3 (mod 4); for n ≡ 1 (mod 4) every merge of two of the four terms is a divisor event = ES(n).
yield: none for n ≡ 1 (mod 4) (the identity covers exactly the classical easy class)
status_ref: Identity verified: 4/n − 4/(n+1) = 4/(n(n+1)) = 2/M. With repeats allowed, the 4-term problem is trivial (cf. PILOT Z1644); FRONTIER §4 item 12 (no relaxation-then-transport without a transport theorem); BRAINSTORM/z1_small_prime_pigeonhole.md (numerators 2, 3 trivial)

role: calibration only (rigidity of prime-reciprocal completions)
missing_theorem: Rigidity lemma: if 4/n − 1/x = Σ_{i≤k} 1/q_i with distinct primes q_i ∤ n, then (Σ_i ∏_{j≠i} q_j)/∏q_i is already in lowest terms, so ∏ q_i equals the reduced denominator of (4x − n)/(nx), forcing every q_i | x; for k = 2 this leaves only x with exactly two prime factors outside n carrying the whole denominator — a sparse, checkable family with no proof role.
status_ref: Elementary (lowest-terms argument); Pass 1: 0 of 76 primes ≤ 400 have a 2-prime completion — consistent with sparsity
